cards.explanation: The answer is the leaders of the tribes. The text calls them "…the leaders of Israel, the heads of their families…" and says they were "…the tribal leaders who had supervised the registration." (Numbers 7:2). These are the men who were already counting heads, and now they come with gifts in their hands. Counting people and then bringing carts is a serious upgrade in job description, friends.

The answer is six covered carts and twelve oxen. The text says they brought "…six covered carts and twelve oxen…" (Numbers 7:3). That's an ox from each leader and a cart from every two leaders, so the math works out clean. Twelve oxen and six carts showing up at once is not a quiet delivery, bakers.

The answer is to accept them for the Tent's work. The LORD tells Moses, "Accept these gifts from them, that they may be used in the work of the Tent of Meeting." (Numbers 7:5). Then He says to give them to the Levites, and Moses does (Numbers 7:6). I know a lot of gifts that end up in a closet, friends, but these ones get a job.

The answer is False. The LORD says to give the carts and oxen to the Levites, "…to each man according to his service." (Numbers 7:5). Some jobs need more carts than others, so the shares are different. Moses follows that, and the Gershonites and Merarites get different amounts (Numbers 7:7-8).

The answer is Ithamar son of Aaron. The text says the Merarites' carts and oxen were "…all under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest." (Numbers 7:8). That's four carts and eight oxen to look after, friends. Somebody had to be the one watching that herd, and I'd have lasted about five minutes before I lost count.

The answer is that they carry the holy objects on their shoulders. The text says the Kohathites get none "…since they were to carry on their shoulders the holy objects for which they were responsible." (Numbers 7:9). Their job was done on foot, with the holy objects on their shoulders. So a cart would not have fit the work, bakers.

The answer is day. The LORD tells Moses, "Each day one leader is to present his offering for the dedication of the altar." (Numbers 7:11). That's twelve leaders across twelve days, one per day. Everybody gets their own turn at the altar, friends, and nobody has to fight for a spot.

The answer is above the mercy seat on the ark. Moses "…heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony." (Numbers 7:89). The text says, "Thus the LORD spoke to him." What a way to end the chapter, friends.
